name: Duchy of Racibórz
alt: Duchy of Opole and Racibórz (1202-1281, with Opole)

predecessors.name: Duchy of Opole
predecessors.text: Racibórz with Cieszyn and Oświęcim, split off the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz in 1281 after the death of Władysław of Opole

successors.name: Duchy of Opole
successors.text: the whole duchy, united with Opole under Jan II the Good in 1521

rulers.name: Nicholas VI, John IV and Valentin (joint)

ledger.x: 1281: the Duchy of Racibórz is split off Opole again.
1290: Mieszko takes Cieszyn and Oświęcim out of Racibórz to found the Duchy of Cieszyn.
1336-1337: the Piast line ends and the duchy passes to the Přemyslid dukes of Opava.
1521: the Duchy of Racibórz is united with the Duchy of Opole under Jan II the Good.
1521: end of the Duchy of Racibórz as a separate duchy, united with Opole; after Jan II's death in 1532 Opole and Racibórz fell to Bohemia.

certainty.note: Neither page opened gives a treaty or survey line; the duchy is a set of named centres (Racibórz, Wodzisław, Żory, Rybnik, Mikołów, Pszczyna) and the Cieszyn and Oświęcim cut-outs are circles.
